item.title: Interactive Planar Arm Kinematics & WebAssembly Simulation
item.author: contact@example.org (Smidr Engineer)
item.description:
Robotic manipulators transform actuator joint angles into spatial tool coordinates. In this interactive guide, we analyze the forward kinematics of a two-link planar robotic manipulator using mathematical derivations, vector diagrams, and real-time in-browser code execution.

1. Mathematical Formulation

Consider a two-link planar arm with joint angles $\theta_1, \theta_2$ and link lengths $l_1, l_2$. The Cartesian coordinates $(x_1, y_1)$ of the elbow joint and $(x_{ee}, y_{ee})$ of the end-effector are governed by trigonometric projection:

$$\begin{aligned} x_1 &= l_1 \cos(\theta_1) \ y_1 &= l_1 \sin(\theta_1) \ x_{ee} &= l_1 \cos(\theta_1) + l_2 \cos(\theta_1 + \theta_2) \ y_{ee} &= l_1 \sin(\theta_1) + l_2 \sin(\theta_1 + \theta_2) \end{aligned}$$

As established by John J. Craig in his foundational robotics treatise [craig2005] , representing these geometric transforms as homogeneous matrices provides computational uniformity for higher degrees of freedom.

2. Kinematic Linkage Diagram (TikZ)

The following schematic is rendered entirely client-side using WebAssembly TeX (TikzJax):

3. Interactive WebAssembly Python Playground

You can modify the joint angles and link lengths in the sandbox below. Click Run (WASM) to compute the end-effector position inside your browser—no backend server computation or cloud latency required!

🔨 Planar Kinematics Solver (Pyodide WASM)
Terminal Output

    

  






4. Including Standalone Source Files


Rather than copy-pasting code into Markdown, Smidr allows referencing clean production scripts directly from your repository using code-file:



    

      

        📄
        kinematics.py
      

      python
    

    
import numpy as np

def forward_kinematics(theta1_deg, theta2_deg, l1=1.0, l2=0.8):
    """
    Computes end-effector (x, y) coordinates for a 2-DOF planar robotic arm.
    :param theta1_deg: Base joint angle in degrees
    :param theta2_deg: Elbow joint angle in degrees
    :param l1: Length of link 1 (meters)
    :param l2: Length of link 2 (meters)
    """
    t1 = np.deg2rad(theta1_deg)
    t2 = np.deg2rad(theta2_deg)
    
    x1 = l1 * np.cos(t1)
    y1 = l1 * np.sin(t1)
    
    x_ee = x1 + l2 * np.cos(t1 + t2)
    y_ee = y1 + l2 * np.sin(t1 + t2)
    
    return (x1, y1), (x_ee, y_ee)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    elbow, ee = forward_kinematics(45.0, 30.0)
    print(f"Elbow Joint Position:  x={elbow[0]:.4f} m, y={elbow[1]:.4f} m")
    print(f"End-Effector Position: x={ee[0]:.4f} m, y={ee[1]:.4f} m")

  



  
💡

  

    
Clean Code Maintenance

    

      By storing algorithms in standalone scripts, your CI test runners can validate your Python code on every commit while your blog renders the exact same file automatically!
    

  






5. Real-Time Parameter Response Tuner


Test closed-loop trajectory tracking response under variable damping ratios and natural frequencies:



  
Robotic Trajectory Response Tuner

  
Adjust velocity gain and damping to observe step response oscillations.

        2.5
      

      
    


    

      

        Damping Ratio (ζ):
        0.45
      

      
    


    

      

        Natural Frequency (ωn):
        3.0
      

      
    

  


  





6. Support Open Science & Robotics Research



  

    

      SPONSOR

Support the Autonomous Systems Lab

        
Our open-source robotics research, simulators, and tutorials are freely published under MIT. Support our ongoing hardware benchmarks and educational tools.

item.title: Quick Start Guide: Writing & Publishing with Smidr
item.author: contact@example.org (Smidr Engineer)
item.description:
Welcome to Smidr—a fast, responsive, and feature-complete Hugo theme designed for researchers, roboticists, engineers, and technical writers. This guide serves as both an interactive tour and a copy-paste reference for all built-in capabilities.

1. Creating Content & Page Bundles

Create a new article bundle directly using the Hugo CLI:

hugo new posts/autonomous-navigation/index.en.md

Using leaf bundles (folder/index.en.md and folder/index.de.md) keeps your images, local scripts, and companion .bib bibliography files neatly organized in the same folder.

2. Dynamic Multilingual Hero & Branding

Smidr supports full internationalization across English and German. You can customize the landing page header badge, subtitle, and description per language in your hugo.yaml:

languages:
  en:
    title: "Jokobus"
    params:
      hero_badge: "ROBOTICS • EMBEDDED SYSTEMS • APPLIED AI"
      subtitle: "Exploring Robotics, Embedded Systems & Applied Machine Learning"
      description: "Field notes, interactive code, and technical deep-dives into modern engineering."
  de:
    title: "Jokobus"
    params:
      hero_badge: "ROBOTIK • EMBEDDED SYSTEMS • ANGEWANDTE KI"
      subtitle: "Praxisnotizen zu Robotik, Embedded Systems & angewandter KI"
      description: "Praxiserprobte Einblicke, interaktiver Code und technische Notizen."

If omitted, Smidr provides localized default fallbacks automatically.

3. LaTeX Mathematics (KaTeX)

Smidr includes client-side KaTeX for instant, zero-latency mathematical typesetting:

  • Inline formulas: Enclose in single dollar signs $f(x) = \sigma(W x + b)$ to render $f(x) = \sigma(W x + b)$.
  • Display equations: Enclose in double dollar signs $$...$$:

$$\mathcal{L}_{PID}(t) = K_p e(t) + K_i \int_0^t e(\tau) d\tau + K_d \frac{de(t)}{dt}$$

4. Code Blocks with One-Click Copy

Standard Markdown code blocks automatically display syntax-highlighted code, language indicators, horizontal scroll containment, and an animated copy button:

// Rust kinematics controller loop
pub fn step_controller(target: f64, current: f64) -> f64 {
    let error = target - current;
    let gain = 1.45;
    gain * error
}

5. Callouts & Admonition Alerts

Highlight critical warnings, pro tips, hardware advice, or theoretical notes using the alert shortcode (or shortcuts tip, note, warning, caution, info, robotics):

💡
Pro Tip
You can pick between 6 distinct alert styling presets: info, note, tip, warning, caution, and robotics.
🤖
Robotics Hardware Safety
Always engage hardware emergency-stop interlocks before enabling high-voltage motor drivers or closed-loop torque control.

6. Client-Side WebAssembly Code Execution

Enable readers to experiment with algorithms directly inside the browser using Pyodide-powered WebAssembly:

🔨 Interactive Python Playground
Terminal Output

    

  








7. Interactive Parameter Widgets & Sliders


Embed interactive HTML5 Canvas visualizers with live parameter sliders to demonstrate dynamic systems and control responses in real time:



  
Dynamic System Response Tuner

  
Adjust damping and natural frequency sliders in real time to observe the step response.


  

    

      

        Proportional Gain (Kp):
        2.5
      

      
    


    

      

        Damping Ratio (ζ):
        0.45
      

      
    


    

      

        Natural Frequency (ωn):
        3.0
      

      
    

  


  







8. Interactive 3D Flashcards


Engage learners with full-width memory flashcards that flip with a smooth 3D CSS rotation on click or tap:



  

    
    

      

        
          💡
          Flashcard
        
        
          ↻
          Click or tap to flip
        
      

      

        What is the Nyquist-Shannon Sampling Theorem?
      

    


    
    

      

        
          ✓
          Answer / Details
        
        
          ↻
          Flip back
        
      

      

        Answer:

A continuous-time bandlimited signal can be perfectly reconstructed from its discrete samples if and only if the sampling frequency exceeds twice the maximum frequency component:

$$f_s > 2 B$$
      

    

  







9. Collapsible Sections & Expandable Bars


Keep long derivations, proofs, or optional exercises clean and organized using collapsible bars (aliases: collapse, details, accordion, spoiler):



  
    
      ▸
      Click to expand the Euler-Lagrange derivation
    
    
      
    
  
  

    
Starting from Hamilton’s principle of least action $\delta S = 0$, where the Lagrangian $\mathcal{L} = T - V$:


$$\frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial \dot{q}_i}\right) - \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial q_i} = Q_i$$


Here, generalized coordinates $q_i$ and non-conservative forces $Q_i$ define the full equation of motion for robotic manipulators.


  







10. Academic Citations & BibTeX Bibliography Engine


Smidr includes a native bibliography engine supporting standard .bib files and inline BibTeX:


    

  1. Automatic .bib Loading: Place a references.bib file inside your post directory. Smidr automatically detects, parses, and formats it.
    2. 

  2. In-Text Citation: Reference keys anywhere in your text using {{< cite "key" >}} or {{< cite "key1,key2" >}}.
    3. 

  3. Citation Popovers: Hovering over any citation badge reveals an instant bibliographic card with author, title, journal, and year.
    4. 

  4. Citation Styles: Switch styles globally in params.yaml or per post in frontmatter:

      

    • numeric: [1]
      • 

    • author-year: (Kalman, 1960)
      • 

    • alphanumeric: [Kal60]
      • 

    

    5. 

  5. Direct BibTeX Export: Every bibliographic entry features a one-click Copy BibTeX button and direct DOI/URL links.
    6. 



Example Citation & Bibliography:


As shown in Kalman’s seminal paper [kalman1960]
 and foundational feedback theory [astrom2010]
, optimal estimation requires minimal variance guarantees.



    

      📚 References & Citations
    

    

      

        Style:
        
        
        
      

      

        
        
      

    

  

    
    
    
      
    

  






11. Interactive Knowledge Graph (Digital Garden)


Connect your thoughts visually! Set gardenGraph: true in your frontmatter or params.yaml to render an interactive physics-simulated network graph at the bottom of the page or on the homepage. Readers can zoom, pan, hover to highlight clusters, and click nodes to navigate directly between interconnected ideas.




12. Contextual Backlinks


When showBacklinks: true is configured, Smidr automatically discovers and displays all incoming references from other articles in your knowledge base, turning your blog into a self-organizing digital garden.




13. Popover Footnotes


Standard Markdown footnotes in Smidr don’t disrupt the reader’s flow1.




14. Command Palette & Instant Fuzzy Search


Press Ctrl + K (or Cmd + K on macOS), or click the search button in the navigation bar or hero section. A modern cyberpunk modal appears instantly, allowing real-time fuzzy querying across article titles, headings, tags, and content snippets.




15. OpenPGP Cryptographic Identity Verification


Display your public cryptographic key, fingerprint, and verification instructions with pgp-card:



  

    

      🔐
      OpenPGP Public Key Verification
    

    RSA 4096 / Ed25519
  


  

    

      

        UID / Identity:
        Smidr Core Engineer <engineer@example.org>
      

      
      

        Key ID:
        0xA1B2C3D4E5F67890
      

      
      
      
      

        Expires:
        Never
      

      
    


    
    

      
Fingerprint:

      

        ABCD1234EF567890ABCD  1234EF567890ABCD1234
        
      

    

    

    
    

      

        ASCII Armored Public Key
        
      

      

-----BEGIN PGP PUBLIC KEY BLOCK-----
Version: OpenPGP.js v5.1.0

mQGNBGXx... [Your ASCII Armored Key Here] ...
-----END PGP PUBLIC KEY BLOCK-----

    

    

    
    

      
        💾
        Download Key (.asc)
      
    

    
  







16. Vector TikZ Diagrams


Render publication-grade TikZ and PGF vector schematics directly in your browser:


{{< tikz caption="Closed-loop feedback control diagram." >}}
\begin{tikzpicture}[auto, node distance=2cm, >=latex]
  \node [input, name=input] {};
  \node [sum, right of=input] (sum) {};
  \node [block, right of=sum] (controller) {Controller};
  \draw [->] (input) -- node {$r(t)$} (sum);
  \draw [->] (sum) -- node {$e(t)$} (controller);
\end{tikzpicture}
{{< /tikz >}}



17. Asciinema Terminal Replay & File Inclusion


    

  • Terminal Recordings: Embed interactive, lightweight terminal sessions without bulky video files:

    {{< asciinema id="123456" title="Deploying Smidr with Hugo" >}}

    • 

  • External Code Files: Reference source code files directly from your repository instead of copy-pasting:

    {{< code-file source="scripts/controller.py" lang="python" title="Controller Implementation" >}}

    • 





18. Secret & Spoiler Reveals


Conceal sensitive solutions or puzzle answers with the secret shortcode:


Verification token: CYBER-SMIDR-2026
 (Hover or tap to reveal)




19. AI Transparency & Provenance Badges


Smidr champions transparent scientific communication. Add provenance metadata to your frontmatter:


used_ai: true
original_language: "de"
original_post_path: "/de/posts/mein-original/"
ai_model: "Claude 3.7 / Ollama"

Smidr automatically renders an unobtrusive provenance notice informing readers whether a post was human-authored, translated, or refined with AI assistance.






    

  1. 

    Hovering or tapping this number opens a sleek popover right in place. Clicking the anchor smoothly jumps with dedicated viewport clearance. ↩︎
    

    2.

item.title: Interactive Client-Side Code Runners with WebAssembly
item.author: contact@example.org (Smidr Engineer)
item.description:
One of the defining innovations of modern technical blogging is allowing readers to tweak parameters, verify equations, and run algorithms directly on the page.

In this dispatch, we demonstrate how Smidr utilizes WebAssembly (Pyodide) to execute code exclusively in the reader’s local web browser.

💡
Server Security & Resilience Guarantee
Because this static site is hosted on a Raspberry Pi (or GitHub Pages), zero code is ever transmitted to or executed on the server. item.title: Autonomous Quadrotor Trajectory Optimization with LQR
item.author: contact@example.org (Smidr Engineer)
item.description:
Designing trajectory controllers for autonomous aerial robotics requires balancing agile maneuverability with dynamic stability. As established in foundational optimal estimation theory by Kalman [kalman1960] and classical feedback principles [astrom2010] , we formulate a linear quadratic regulator (LQR) for a 6-DOF multi-rotor system1.

Mathematical Formulation

The linearized continuous-time error dynamics around the hover equilibrium point are expressed via state-space representation:

$$\dot{x}(t) = A x(t) + B u(t)$$

where the state vector $x \in \mathbb{R}^{12}$ represents position, velocities, Euler angles, and body angular rates:

$$x = \begin{bmatrix} p_x & p_y & p_z & \dot{p}_x & \dot{p}_y & \dot{p}_z & \phi & \theta & \psi & p & q & r \end{bmatrix}^T$$

The optimal control law minimizes the infinite-horizon quadratic performance index:

$$J = \int_{0}^{\infty} \left( x^T Q x + u^T R u \right) dt$$

The continuous algebraic Riccati equation (CARE) is solved to compute the feedback gain matrix $K$:

$$A^T P + P A - P B R^{-1} B^T P + Q = 0 \implies u(t) = -K x(t) = -R^{-1} B^T P x(t)$$

🤖
Actuator Saturation Warning
Rotational motor velocities are physically bounded by maximum ESC voltage. Saturation $u_{max}$ must be handled with anti-windup clamping to prevent destabilizing non-linear limit cycles.

Control Architecture (Vector TikZ Diagram)

Below is the closed-loop feedback architecture rendered in vectorized SVG directly in your browser using TikZ WebAssembly:

Interactive Control Tuner

You can adjust the damping ratio $\zeta$ and proportional gain $K_p$ in the live system simulator below to observe the pole placement and step response settling time:

Second-Order Closed-Loop Step Response
Drag the sliders below to witness closed-loop damping and transient oscillations in real time.
Proportional Gain (Kp): 2.5
Damping Ratio (ζ): 0.45
Natural Frequency (ωn): 3.0

Secret Telemetry Flag

Here is an encrypted debug marker embedded in this dispatch: KEY-90812-AUTONOMOUS-ROVER-DEPLOYED (Notice how the text above is invisible until you highlight or hover it with your mouse cursor!)

Code Implementation (Python / NumPy)

Below is the state-space feedback loop computation with syntax highlighting, horizontal scrolling, and a copy button:

import numpy as np
import scipy.linalg

def compute_lqr_gain(A: np.ndarray, B: np.ndarray, Q: np.ndarray, R: np.ndarray):
    """Solve Continuous Algebraic Riccati Equation (CARE) and return gain K."""
    P = scipy.linalg.solve_continuous_are(A, B, Q, R)
    K = np.linalg.inv(R) @ (B.T @ P)
    return K, P

# Hover linearized system matrices
A = np.zeros((12, 12))
A[0:3, 3:6] = np.eye(3)
B = np.zeros((12, 4))
B[5, :] = 1.0 / 1.25 # Mass normalized thrust

Q = np.diag([10, 10, 20, 1, 1, 2, 5, 5, 5, 0.1, 0.1, 0.1])
R = np.eye(4) * 0.1

K, P = compute_lqr_gain(A, B, Q, R)
print("Optimal LQR Gain Shape:", K.shape)
